title: Kumamoto 2026: two scarce teams, four conflicting reports
disclosure: The earthquake, map geometry, instrument readings, and mapped landslide polygons are public observations. Every report about people and every dispatch outcome is synthetic exercise data. This is a deterministic product demonstration, not a claim about the real emergency response.

exercise.question: With only two assessment teams, which two reported sites should receive them first?
exercise.one_changed_variable: The orchestration graph. Both arms receive identical reports, truth, resources, time, and deterministic policies.

agents.role: Normalize incoming reports without deciding whether they are true.
Keep claim versions, sources, contradictions, and freshness separate.
Rank legally eligible sites against the shared resource limit.
Issue idempotent dispatches and record exact effect receipts.
Reveal synthetic outcomes and score both arms.

graphs.plain_english: Read every report, keep the largest number reported for each site, then send the two teams to the two largest numbers.
Read every report, keep competing versions separate, compare independent sources, reject or hold weak versions, then rank only current supported claims and record why every dispatch happened.

metrics.formula: Sum the frozen synthetic outcome for every uniquely dispatched target.
Count dispatches whose matched exercise claim version is rejected by the shared evidence comparison.
Divide selected supported claim versions by all dispatched claim versions.
